b: As anglers, it’s easy to spend much of our time looking ahead. We’re thinking about the next fishing trip, scouting a new lake, dreaming about a personal best, or adding another bait to an already crowded tackle box. There’s always another season to prepare for, another adventure to plan, and another fish to chase.

But Thanksgiving offers an opportunity to slow down and take stock of what really matters. Beyond the boats, tackle, and time on the water, we’re reminded that our greatest blessings often have little to do with fishing. They’re found in the health of the people we love, the family gathered around the table, the friendships we’ve built, and the simple moments that become our most treasured memories.

This year, our team is reflecting on the people, experiences, and moments we’re most grateful for. From family and health to careers, friendships, and time spent outdoors, these are the things that make life meaningful — and give us all the more reason to be thankful when we get back out on the water.

I am incredibly thankful for my sister and the strength, courage, and resilience she has shown through a challenging chapter in her life. We have known about her mitral valve prolapse since she was a teenager, but recently, a condition she had lived with for so long reached a point where surgery became necessary. Watching her navigate that uncertainty and face surgery was a reminder of how precious life and family truly are.

I am grateful that she came through it and that we can look ahead with her healthy and by our side. Experiences like this have a way of putting life into perspective, reminding us not to take a single day, a family gathering, or even a simple conversation for granted. I am proud of her and deeply thankful for the memories we still have to make together.

Above all, I am thankful for my wife and son and the time we share as a family. Some of my most cherished memories come from the simplest moments spent on the water or enjoying the outdoors together. Whether we’re boating, fishing, exploring new places, or simply taking in the beauty around us, these are the experiences that mean the most. As the seasons change, I know I’ll be dreaming of family canoe rides all winter long.

Sitting at the children’s hospital waiting for my 5-year-old to have blood work done, I realized there’s plenty to be thankful for than just fishing. Instead of brainstorming new lakes to fish, or day dreaming about a new bait or PB, my mind was far from the water. She was there to have some tests done on a fever that continued to persist for too many days. You better believe how thankful I was when those blood results came back negative, but I probably won’t forget the moment when she looked directly at us and asked “What are they doing to me?” as the techs drew blood.

So during this Thanksgiving holiday, I’m giving thanks to the health of my family and friends. And especially for the health of those little people who call you Mom or Dad; the sponges who rely on you and mirror you every single day. To anyone who might not be a parent or caregiver, give those special people around you grace and support too. Some of the stories I’ve heard from working within the fishing industry related to the health of loved ones are both heartbreaking and inspiring. Many aren’t publicized, and I’ve recognized that many folks are fighting battles or struggles that are mostly hidden. This year I say cheers to health, empathy, and hogs over 7 pounds.

Thanksgiving Eve means we’re just shy of my one-year anniversary here — and life has given me tons to be grateful for in those 359 days, starting with the gift of finally deleting all the job-search apps I’ve haunted for years.

My word-nerd career turned 20 years old this past June. Those two decades have taken me from local news to the livery industry, and from finance to now fishing, so I’ve gotten to learn about oodles of things that I never thought would pique my curiosity. I’ve had a blast diving into a whole new-to-me world here. And I am endlessly grateful to be surrounded by topic-expert colleagues who are wonderfully generous in sharing their wealth of knowledge as I’ve settled in.

Beyond work, my husband and I are celebrating 20 years together (today, in fact!) after enjoying our 17th wedding anniversary earlier this month. Our beloved 13-year-old pooch gave us some serious medical scares this year, but he’s bounced back like only a cattle dog can and is just as feisty as ever. I taught figure skating classes for the first time and discovered just how rewarding it is to cheer on other adults as they realize that they can do the hard thing if they just trust themselves and the process — which I think is a lesson we’re never too old to challenge ourselves with. And I’ve absolutely trounced my reading goals for this year!

I get to meet another holiday season happy where I am in life and pleased with the quiet joys it’s given me: I can’t ask for anything better than that peace. Not all years are this kind, and I am profoundly grateful that this one was.
